`precisedelta()` now keeps the sign of a negative value. `precisedelta(timedelta(seconds=-3661))` returns `'-1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second'`.

The full suite passes with doctests included (770 passed, 112 skipped). The new negative-sign tests fail on the base commit (7 failures) and pass with the fix.

- **The fix:** in `src/humanize/time.py`, the function notes whether the input was negative. It adds `-` to the finished string only when the string has a nonzero digit, so zero never gains a sign. That includes a tiny negative value that rounds to zero, like `timedelta(seconds=-0.1)` with `minimum_unit="minutes"`, which stays `'0 minutes'`.
- **Scope:** the rule applies to a `timedelta` or a plain number of seconds, for every `minimum_unit`, `suppress` and `format`. I did not add sign handling for `datetime` inputs.
- **Docstring:** I added one negative example.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_time.py` has a parametrized test that checks `precisedelta(-x) == "-" + precisedelta(x)` across several units, suppressions and formats. A second test checks that zero has no sign.

While checking the base commit I ran `git stash` by mistake, which is against the worktree rules. I restored my changes with `git stash apply` and dropped the entry, so the worktree holds only the two edited files. Afterwards I ran the base-commit check against a copy of the original source in `$TMPDIR`.
